title: MIPPE Scale Validation Protocol
author: Emmanuelle Dufait
materials: Paramedical professionals (speech therapists, educators, psychomotor therapists)
Read the MIPPE scale presentation and scoring instructions
Rated each video using the 9-item MIPPE scale

steps.title: Perform Preliminary Rating of Video Corpus
steps.instruction: The lead researcher (E. Dufait) must rate all 228 PERL videos using the MIPPE scale to familiarize with item functioning, identify ambiguities for scale refinement, and classify videos into 'good', 'average', and 'poor' interaction categories.

steps.title: Select Representative Videos
steps.instruction: Select videos for the psychometric validation sample based on representativeness of interaction quality levels, technical quality (image stability, audio clarity), and diversity of caregiver-child dyad characteristics.

steps.title: Recruit Professional Raters
steps.instruction: Recruit a minimum of 100 professional raters through professional networks, institutional contacts, and social media, targeting a minimum of 5–10 participants per item.

substeps.instruction: Target physicians (psychiatrists, pediatricians, child psychiatrists, general practitioners, PMI physicians, midwives).
Target nurses and child nurses (nurses, psychiatric nurses, pediatric nurses, advanced practice nurses, child nurses).

steps.title: Execute Rating Procedure via Online Platform
steps.instruction: Direct participants to the dedicated online platform via a unique URL for voluntary, anonymous rating.

substeps.instruction: Randomly assign each participant one panel of 6 videos (all at 4 months, representing good, average, and poor interaction quality).
Collect sociodemographic information (profession, years of experience, type of clinical population).
Ensure each rater assesses the same panel of 6 videos.

steps.title: Manage Data Collection
steps.instruction: Transmit rating data from the online platform to a secure email, enter into a structured database, and pseudonymize the data.

substeps.instruction: Exclude data from raters who did not complete all 6 ratings.

steps.title: Perform Descriptive Analyses
steps.instruction: Analyze the distribution of responses for each MIPPE item across the final sample (N = 143 raters, 858 total ratings).

substeps.instruction: Conduct Shapiro-Wilk tests for normality at the item and total score levels.
Perform Levene's test for homogeneity of variances.

steps.title: Evaluate Content Validity and Internal Consistency
steps.instruction: Assess internal consistency using specific statistical thresholds.

substeps.instruction: Calculate McDonald's omega for non-normal Likert data.

steps.title: Evaluate Construct Validity and Factor Structure
steps.instruction: Determine the factor structure of the scale using Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA).

substeps.instruction: Perform EFA using a polychoric correlation matrix, assessing sampling adequacy via Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) index and Bartlett's test of sphericity, and using the eigenvalue ≥ 1 criterion for factor retention.
Perform CFA using the lavaan package with DWLS estimator, evaluating fit indices: CFI (target ≥ 0.95), TLI (target ≥ 0.95), RMSEA (target ≤ 0.06), SRMR (target ≤ 0.08), and chi-square p-value.

steps.title: Assess Discriminant Validity
steps.instruction: Determine if MIPPE scores differ across professional backgrounds and experience levels.

substeps.instruction: Perform a two-factor ANOVA (socio-professional category × interaction quality), expecting a significant effect of interaction quality (p < 0.05) and a non-significant effect of professional category.
Perform Levene's test for homogeneity of variances between professional groups.
Conduct seniority analysis comparing scores across experience levels using a threshold of 11 years.

steps.title: Assess Convergent and Divergent Validity
steps.instruction: Calculate Pearson correlations between MIPPE total scores and external variables.

substeps.instruction: Convergent: Correlate with maternal education level, 'desired child' variable, Revised Brunet-Lézine developmental scale (language subscale), and ADBB (alarm détresse bébé) scale at 4 months (N = 121) and 24 months (N = 107).
Divergent: Correlate with the presence of addiction in the family (expected negative correlation).

steps.title: Determine Clinical Thresholds
steps.instruction: Optimize classification into three quality categories by comparing threshold combinations, prioritizing sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Apply final thresholds: ≤ 15 (poor interaction, intervention recommended), 16–20 (average, monitoring recommended), and ≥ 20 (good quality).
